newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight rate firmer on weekend covering.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight rate firmer on weekend covering.

text.p: * Interbank average rate rises to 11.71875 pct
The Philippine interbank call loan rate inched higher to 11.71875 percent against Friday's 11.0625 percent on weekend reserves covering, traders said.
"The market was a bit tight because of higher peso demand to cover banks' three-day reserve deficiencies," a trader said.
On the supply side, the liquidity was supported by 1.0 billion peso net inflow arising from the dollar purchases of Central Bank in the foreign exchange market last Friday.
Volume turnover was moderate at 23.784 billion with done rates ranging from 11.0 percent to 12.78125 percent.
Twenty-seven borrowers tapped the overnight market for funds with 34 others providing the liquidity.
The secondary government securities market was active with buyers trying to park their funds in higher-yielding Treasury bills.
Effective yields were seven to 10 basis points lower than the average rates registered in the previous auction.
Traders expected the auction rates to stay sideways in the three and six month bills, and slightly lower in the one-year bills after the auction committee adjusted the offer volume.
The committee reduced its offer for one-year bills to 2.5 billion pesos from 3.5 billion pesos.
The committee raised the volume for three-month bills to 1.5 billion pesos from 1.0 billion pesos and six-month bills to 2.0 billion from 1.5 billion pesos.
The auction is set for Monday afternoon.
